en: An explicit set of requirements to be satisfied by a material, product, or service.
An act of specifying.

specification.ety: From Middle French specification, from Medieval Latin specificationem (accusative of specificatio).

ex.en: It is a new model with improved specifications.
ex.ja: 新モデルとなりスペックが刷新された。

ex.en: Specifications and price are subject to change.
ex.ja: 仕様、価格は変更することがあります。

ex.en: Any industrial property rights relating to the Product Specification shall belong to ABC Inc.
ex.ja: 製品仕様にかかわる一切の工業所有権はＡＢＣ社に帰属するものとする。

en: Possessing or displaying splendor; shining; very bright.
Gorgeous; magnificent; sumptuous; of remarkable beauty.

ex.ja: 王は壮麗な宮殿で有名だった。

ex.en: We had a splendid holiday in Sweden.
ex.ja: 私達はスウェーデンで素敵な休日を送った。

ex.en: We had a splendid dinner that evening.
ex.ja: その晩私達はすばらしいディナーを食べた。

en: A monocular optical instrument that magnifies distant objects, especially in astronomy.
Any instrument used in astronomy for observing distant objects (such as a radio telescope).
To extend or contract in the manner of a telescope.
To slide or pass one within another, after the manner of the sections of a small telescope or spyglass.

telescope.ety:
From tele- + -scope.
From Latin tēlescopium, from Ancient Greek τηλεσκόπος (tēleskópos, “far-seeing”), from τῆλε (têle, “afar”) + σκοπέω (skopéō, “to look at”).
Coined in 1611 by the Greek mathematician Giovanni Demisiani for one of Galileo Galilei's instruments presented at a banquet at the Accademia dei Lincei. Doublet of Telescopium.

ex.en: The girl had a telescope in her hand.
ex.ja: その女の子は手に望遠鏡を持っていた。

ex.en: He looked at the ship through his telescope.
ex.ja: 彼は望遠鏡を使ってその船を眺めた。

ex.en: You can see stars with a telescope.
ex.ja: 望遠鏡で星を見ることができますよ。

note.ja: tele（遠く）+ scope（見る）。遠くを見る道具 →「望遠鏡」。microscope（顕微鏡）と対。

en: To measure or check the temperature of something, especially food or equipment in a commercial kitchen.
Synonym of temporary (“short-term employee”).
Synonym of temporary (“short-term variable”).

ex.en: "Manpower" is the world's largest temp agency.
ex.ja: マンパワーは世界で一番大きな人材派遣会社です。

ex.en: She is a temp.
ex.ja: 彼女は派遣社員です。

en: Any material made of interlacing or matted fibres, including carpeting and geotextiles, woven or nonwoven.
A non-nudist.
Clothing compulsive.

textile.ety: Borrowed from Latin textile, substantive use of textilis (“woven”), from texō (“weave”).

ex.en: Circumstances surrounding the textile industry have changed.
ex.ja: 繊維産業をとりまく状況は変化した。

ex.en: Does that store keep textile goods?
ex.ja: あの店には織物類が置いてありますか。

ex.en: Scotland is famous for its woollen textiles.
ex.ja: スコットランドは毛織物で有名だ。

en: The property of being thick (in dimension).
A measure of how thick (in dimension) something is.
To trim (wood) to a consistent thickness using a thickness planer.

thickness.ety: From Middle English thikkenesse, thiknesse, from Old English þicnes (“thickness, viscosity, density, hardness; obscurity, cloud, darkness; thicket; depth, a thick body, anything thick or heavy”), from Proto-West Germanic *þikkwīnassī (“thickness”), equivalent to thick + -ness. Cognate with West Frisian tsjokkens (“thickness”), Old High German dickinessī, dikkinissi, diknissi (“thickness, density”). Eclipsed non-native Middle English crassitude (“thickness”) from Latin crassitūdō (“thickness”).

en: A small, typically rectangular or round, flat, and rigid object upon which things are carried.
The items on a full tray.
to place (items) on a tray
to slide down a snow-covered hill on a tray from a cafeteria.

tray.ety: From Middle English trey, from Old English trēġ, trīġ (“wooden board, tray”), from Proto-West Germanic *trauwi, from Proto-Germanic *trawją (“wooden vessel”), from Proto-Indo-European *drewo-, *dóru (“tree; wood”). Cognate with Old Norse treyja (“carrier”), Old Swedish trø (“wooden grain measure”), Low German Treechel (“dough trough”), Ancient Greek δροίτη (droítē, “tub, vat”), Sanskrit द्रोण (droṇa, “trough”). Related to trough and tree.

ex.en: She set the tray down on the table.
ex.ja: 彼女はテーブルの上に皿を置いた。

ex.en: I need one tray of eggs, you see.
ex.ja: １パック卵がいるんだ。

ex.en: He made his sister a nice pen tray.
ex.ja: 彼は妹に素敵なペン皿を作ってあげた。

en: Without the ability to reason; unreasoning.
Not reasonable; going beyond what could be expected or asked for.

unreasonable.ety: From Middle English unresonable, equivalent to un- + reasonable, originally partly after Latin irratiōnābilis.

ex.en: My heart is beating at an unreasonable rate.
ex.ja: めちゃくちゃ心臓が動く。

ex.en: He cannot have said such an unreasonable thing.
ex.ja: 彼がそんな筋の通らないことを言ったはずはない。

ex.en: You must not give in to his unreasonable demands.
ex.ja: あなたは彼の不当な要求に屈してはいけない。

en: uncertain, ambivalent.
unstable or precarious

unsure.ety: From Middle English unsure, equivalent to un- + sure. Piecewise doublet of insecure and unsecure.

ex.en: Lately, prices have gone up, so I'm unsure whether to buy again.
ex.ja: 最近高くなってきて、また買うか迷う。

ex.en: I'm unsure of the regularity.
ex.ja: その規則性がよく分からないんだよな。

en: US, Canada, and Oxford British English standard spelling of utilise.

utilize.ety: From French utiliser, from Italian utilizzare, from utile (“useful”), from Latin ūtilis, from ūtī (“use”).

ex.en: We had better utilize our natural resources.
ex.ja: 我々は天然資源をもっと有効に利用する必要がある。

ex.en: Try to utilize your leisure for reading.
ex.ja: 余暇を読書に利用するように努めなさい。

ex.en: Atomic energy can be utilized for peaceful purposes.
ex.ja: 原子力エネルギーを平和のために利用することができる。

en: An estimation of something's worth.
The process of estimating the value of a financial asset or liability.

valuation.ety: From Middle French valuation, noun of action from valuer, from Old French valoir.

ex.en: Experts put a high valuation on the painting.
ex.ja: 専門家はその絵に高い評価を下した。

A worker unit.

en: To break or disregard (a rule or convention).
To rape.

violate.ety: From Middle English violaten (“to defile, render impure”), from violat(e) (“defiled, desecrated”, also used as the past participle of violaten) + -en, borrowed from Latin violātus, perfect passive participle of violō (“to treat with violence (whether bodily or mental)”), see -ate (verb-forming suffix). Ultimately from vīs (“strength, power, force, violence”).

ex.en: He was accused of having violated the law.
ex.ja: 彼は法を犯したかどで訴えられた。

ex.en: I will never violate a law again.
ex.ja: 僕は決して法律を破ることはしない。

ex.en: The company is violating multiple labor laws.
ex.ja: 会社は複数の労働法に違反している。

en: Clear, detailed, or powerful.
Bright, intense, or colourful.
A felt-tipped permanent marker; a marker pen.

The noun sense (a type of marker pen) was genericized from Bic's Vivid Marker brand.

ex.en: She painted a vivid picture of the event.
ex.ja: 彼女はその事件を生き生きとした筆致で描写した。

ex.en: The event still remains vivid in my memory.
ex.ja: その出来事は今でも私の記憶に生々しく残っている。

ex.en: The accident is still vivid in his memory.
ex.ja: その事故はまだありありと彼の記憶に残っている。

note.ja: viv（生きる）+ id。生き生きした →「鮮やかな・生々しい」。

That which is allocated; allowance, entitlement.

allocation.ety: From Middle French allocacion, from Medieval Latin allocātiō. By surface analysis, allocate + -ion.

An activity that is entertaining or amusing, such as dancing, gunning, or fishing.

ex.ja: 村には娯楽がない。

en: Any substance that can destroy or inhibit the growth of bacteria and similar microorganisms, generally transported by the lymphatic system.
Of or relating to antibiotics.

antibiotic.ety: Borrowed from French antibiotique; by surface analysis, anti- + -biotic.

ex.en: Keep taking this antibiotic until it is gone.
ex.ja: 抗生物質はなくなるまで飲んでください。

ex.en: The doctor dosed the girl with antibiotics.
ex.ja: 医者は少女に抗生物質を服用させた。

ex.en: I'll prescribe some antibiotics.
ex.ja: 抗生物質を処方しましょう。

en: The act of anticipating, taking up, placing, or considering something beforehand, or before the proper time in natural order.
The eagerness associated with waiting for something to occur.

anticipation.ety: From Middle English anticipacioun, from Middle French anticipation and its etymon Latin anticipātiō, anticipātiōnem. By surface analysis, anticipate + -ion.

ex.en: We wait in anticipation of meeting.
ex.ja: お待ちしております。

ex.en: Mother took the clothes off the line in anticipation of rain.
ex.ja: 母は雨が来そうだと言って洗濯物をとりこんだ。

ex.en: An exhibition was given in anticipation of the Queen's visit.
ex.ja: 女王の訪問を見越して展示会が開催された。

en: Having excessive pride in oneself, often with contempt or disrespect for others.

arrogant.ety: From Middle English arrogaunt, from Old French arrogant, from Latin arrogāns, present active participle of arrogō.

ex.en: No woman is as arrogant as she is.
ex.ja: 彼女ほど傲慢な女性はいない。

ex.en: I couldn't put up with her arrogant behavior.

en: Helping; giving assistance or support.
Supplementary or subsidiary.
A person or group that acts in an auxiliary manner.
A sailing vessel equipped with an engine.

auxiliary.ety: From Latin auxiliārius (“assistant, ally”), equiv. to auxiliāris (“helping, aiding”), from auxilium (“help, aid”), from augēre (“to increase”).

en: Portable cases, large bags, and similar equipment for manually carrying, pushing, or pulling personal items while traveling
Factors, especially psychological ones, which interfere with a person's ability to function effectively.

baggage.ety: From Middle English bagage, from Old French bagage, baguage, from bague (“bundle, sack”), of Germanic/North Germanic origin, probably from the same ultimate source as Old Norse baggi (“pack, bundle”). Compare also bag. By surface analysis, bag + -age. The old meaning of "nasty woman" likely derives from the sense of "something awkward to be carried" (compare faggot).

ex.en: She took two pieces of baggage with her.
ex.ja: 彼女は手荷物を２個持っていった。

ex.en: She took a lot of baggage with her.
ex.ja: 彼女は手荷物をたくさん持って行った。

ex.en: She had her baggage carried to the airport.
ex.ja: 彼女は荷物を空港まで運んでもらった。

en: A signal fire to notify of the approach of an enemy, or to give any notice, commonly of warning.
A signal, buoy, post, or other conspicuous mark erected on an eminence near the shore, or moored in shoal water, as a guide to mariners, …
To act as a beacon.
To give light to, as a beacon; to light up; to illumine.

From Middle English beken, from Old English bēacn (“sign, signal”), from Proto-West Germanic *baukn, from Proto-Germanic *baukną, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂u-, *bʰeh₂- (“to shine”).
Doublet of buoy. Compare West Frisian beaken (“buoy”), Dutch baken (“beacon”), Middle Low German bāke (“beacon, sign”), German Bake (“traffic sign”), Middle High German bouchen (“sign”).

en: Generosity; also (countable) an act of generosity.
Something given liberally; a gift.
To offer a monetary reward for the capturing or killing of.

bounty.ety: From Middle English bounte (“goodness, virtue; beauty; strength; chivalry, valour; excellence; kindness, mercy; good deed; generosity”) [and other forms], borrowed from Anglo-Norman bounté and Old French bonté, bontet, bunté (modern French bonté (“goodness, kindness”)), from Latin bonitās.

ex.en: Tom always dreamed of becoming a bounty hunter.
ex.ja: トムは常々、賞金稼ぎになりたいと夢見ていた。

en: A participant in a boxing match: a fighter who boxes.
A type of internal combustion engine in which cylinders are arranged in two banks on either side of a single crankshaft.

ex.en: The boxer tried to keep his head down.
ex.ja: そのボクサーは体重を抑えておく努力をした。

ex.en: The boxer lost his weight for the match.
ex.ja: そのボクサーは試合のために体重を減らした。

ex.en: The boxer received a blow to the body.
ex.ja: そのボクサーはボディーに一撃食らった。

en: Made of material produced by the high-temperature firing of inorganic, nonmetallic rocks and minerals.
A hard, brittle, inorganic, nonmetallic material, made by firing a material such as clay at a high temperature.
An object made of this material.

ceramic.ety: From Ancient Greek κεραμικός (keramikós, “potter's”), from κέραμος (kéramos, “potter's clay”), perhaps from a pre-Hellenic word or from Proto-Indo-European *kerh₂- (“to heat, burn, fire”).

ex.en: I have an interest in oriental ceramics.
ex.ja: 東洋の陶器に興味があります。

en: A type of grass (such as wheat, rice or oats) cultivated for its edible grains.
The grains of such a grass.
Of or relating to cereal.

cereal.ety: Borrowed from French céréale (“having to do with cereal”), from Latin Cerealis (“of or relating to Ceres”), from Ceres (“Roman goddess of agriculture”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱer- (“grow”), from which also Latin sincerus (English sincere) and Latin crēscō (“grow”) (English crescent). The adjective is equivalent to Cere(s) + -al.

ex.en: I ate cereal for breakfast.
ex.ja: 朝食は、シリアルでした。

ex.en: I eat cereal for breakfast.
ex.ja: 朝食にはシリアルを食べます。

ex.en: He quickly ate some cereal and a banana.
ex.ja: 彼はシリアルとバナナをペロリと平らげた。

en: One who challenges.
One who confronts or opposes; a confronter, an opposer.

challenger.ety:
Inherited from Middle English chalengere, chalangeour, chalenger (“one who causes injury, or makes false charges or slanderous statements; one who disputes, disputant, objector; claimant”), and then partly from both of the following:
* From Middle English chalengen (“to accuse; to accuse falsely or maliciously, slander; to treat unjustly, wrong; to dispute, object; to make a claim or demand; to rebuke, scold; to issue a challenge to; etc.”) + -er, -ere (suffix forming agent nouns). Chalengen is derived from Anglo-Norman chalenger, and Old French chalenger, chalongier (“to challenge, dispute; t

ex.en: The champion had the challengers at his mercy.
ex.ja: チャンピオンは挑戦者たちを思うままにあしらった。

ex.en: He looked the toughest of all the challengers.
ex.ja: 挑戦者の中で彼が一番強そうに見えた。

ex.en: He's mowed down a parade of challengers before.
ex.ja: 彼はこれまでいとも簡単にたくさんの挑戦者をリングに沈めてきた。

en: A body of persons, such as priests, who are trained and ordained for religious service.

clergy.ety: From Middle English clergie (attested in the 13th century), from Old French clergie (“learned men”), from Late Latin clēricātus, from Latin clēricus (“one ordained for religious services”), from Ancient Greek κληρικός (klērikós, “of the clergy”). Equivalent to cleric + -ate.

ex.en: All the clergy are against the new law.
ex.ja: すべての牧師が新しい法律に反対である。

en: The kola plant, genus Cola, famous for its nut, or one of these nuts.
A beverage or a drink made with kola nut flavoring, caramel and carbonated water.

cola.ety: From a Niger-Congo language, compare Temne kola, Mandinka kola. The beverage "Coca-Cola" was what made the term widely known, and popularized the spelling with c instead of k.

ex.en: This cola has gone flat and doesn't taste good.
ex.ja: このコーラ、炭酸が抜けちゃっておいしくない。

ex.en: I like cola better than coffee.
ex.ja: コーヒーよりコーラの方が好きだ。

ex.en: I prefer cola to coffee.
ex.ja: コーヒーよりコーラの方が好きだ。

en: A state of unconsciousness from which one may not wake up, usually induced by some form of trauma.

coma.ety: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek κῶμα (kôma, “deep sleep”).

ex.en: The patient is in a deep coma.
ex.ja: 患者は深い昏睡状態にあります。

ex.en: Is Tom in a coma?
ex.ja: トムは昏睡状態なんですか？

ex.en: Unfortunately, my neighbor had a traffic accident and fell into a coma.
ex.ja: 隣人は残念ながら交通事故に遭って、昏睡状態になってしまった。

en: In a comfortable manner.
Easily; without effort or difficulty.

comfortably.ety:
Etymology tree

Middle English -ly
English -ly
English comfortably
From comfortable + -ly.

ex.en: We are comfortably established in our new home.
ex.ja: 我々は快適な新居に落ち着いた。

ex.en: I want to live comfortably when I become old.
ex.ja: 老後は楽に暮らしたい。

ex.en: I completed the university course comfortably.
ex.ja: しっかりと大学の課程を終えました。

en: A magnetic or electronic device used to determine the cardinal directions (usually magnetic or true north).
A pair of compasses (a device used to draw circular arcs and transfer length measurements).
To surround; to encircle; to environ; to stretch round.
To go about or round entirely; to traverse.

compass.ety: From Middle English compas (“a circle, circuit, limit, form, a mathematical instrument”), from Old French compas, from Medieval Latin compassus (“a circle, a circuit”), from Latin com- (“together”) + passus (“a pace, step, later a pass, way, route”); see pass, pace.

ex.en: I don't know how to use this compass.
ex.ja: 私は、この羅針盤の使い方を知りません。

ex.en: This is beyond the compass of my ability.
ex.ja: これは私の力では無理です。

ex.en: Do they have something like a compass?
ex.ja: 彼らは方位磁石のようなものをもっているのですか。

note.ja: com（共に）+ pass（歩み）。歩幅で測る道具 →「コンパス・方位磁石・範囲」。

en: The state or act of contemning; the feeling or attitude of regarding someone or something as inferior, base, or worthless; scorn, disdain.
The state of being despised or dishonored; disgrace.

contempt.ety: From Latin contemptus (“scorn”), from contemnō (“to scorn, despise”), from com- + temnō (“to despise”). Displaced native Old English forsewennes.

ex.en: I feel nothing but contempt for such behavior.
ex.ja: 私はそのような態度には軽蔑以外の何物にも感じない。

ex.en: He always speaks of the government with contempt.
ex.ja: 彼はいつも政府を侮ったようなことを言う。

ex.en: I have a fine contempt for him.
ex.ja: 私は彼をひどく軽蔑している。

note.ja: con（完全に）+ temp（軽んじる）+ t。ラテン語 contemnere（さげすむ）から →「軽蔑・侮辱」。

en: Documentary evidence of someone's right to credit or authority, especially such a document given to an ambassador by a country.
login data

ex.en: He has good credentials as a conductor.
